title: You keep working with your agent as before. Chock checks each action before it lands.

context.name: Context
context.line: rules files such as AGENTS.md, skills, memory

hook.name: Hook point
hook.line: the harness asks before a tool runs

tools.name: Tools
tools.line: edit file, write file, run command, git

chock.name: Chock
chock.line: a local program; its rules are files in your repository; no model, no tokens

connectors.name: Into context
connectors.line: a short rules block Chock writes into AGENTS.md. Advisory.

connectors.name: At the hook point
connectors.line: Chock judges the proposed tool call: allow, ask or block. A refusal goes back to the model with one line on what to do instead.

connectors.name: In CI
connectors.line: the same gates on the pull request.

stops.line: a password or API key written into code
a container that runs as root or uses a floating image tag such as latest
a download piped straight into a shell
data sent to a host you have not approved
the agent weakening the checks that review its work (asks you first)

footer: The rules are files in your repository. A person turns them on once with chock sync.
alt: A layered sketch: you ask a coding agent for a change; inside the agent a model and an agent loop work with context, and the loop's tool calls pass a hook point before the tools run. Chock sits below with four connectors: a rules block in the agent's context, a judgement at the hook point where the agent has hooks, the git hook at commit and the same gates in CI.
